sources.entry: nox - Flexible test automation for Python.

summary.one_liner: Nox is a command-line tool that automates testing across multiple Python environments, configured through a standard Python file rather than an INI-style config.
summary.what_it_does: Nox runs test and lint automation in multiple Python environments, similar to tox. Sessions are defined as Python functions decorated with @nox.session, and each session can install packages and run commands inside its environment. The README's example defines a "tests" session that installs and runs pytest and a "lint" session that runs flake8. Users can list all sessions, view a session's usage docstring, run every session, or run a single named session from the command line. The README says it is meant to be installed globally, recommended via pipx or pip, rather than inside a project virtual environment. The README links to external documentation for further details.
use_cases: automate pytest runs across Python versions
run linting sessions like flake8 in isolated environments
replace tox with a Python-file configuration
run a single named test session from the command line
list and document available test sessions
notable: Configuration is a standard Python file with @nox.session decorated functions instead of a separate config format
Alternative to tox with the same goal of multi-environment test automation
Sessions can carry docstrings that are shown via 'nox --usage'
Recommended installation via pipx to keep the CLI separate from project environments
caveats: README is brief and defers most detail to external documentation links, which are not included in the text provided
Designed to be installed globally rather than inside a project virtual environment
keywords: run tests in multiple python versions
